answer:
The first nominated African American presidential candidate was **Frederick Douglass**, who received one vote at the **1888 Republican National Convention** as a presidential nominee (making him the first African American to be nominated by a major political party for President).

At the time of this historic nomination in June 1888, Frederick Douglass's spouse was **Helen Pitts Douglass**. 

Douglass had been married to his first wife, Anna Murray Douglass, from 1838 until her death in 1882. After Anna's passing, he married Helen Pitts in 1884. Helen was an educated white abolitionist and suffragist, and their marriage was notable for being interracial during the Reconstruction era. They remained married until Helen's death in 1903.
